This paper examines Constraint Handling Rules (CHR), a declarative language for constraint systems, by analyzing its expressiveness. We demonstrate that the expressiveness of CHR is contingent upon the atom count within rules' heads. Specifically, we establish that CHR utilizing a finite set of rules over a finite domain is equivalent to finite automata when a fixed number of atoms is employed in rule heads. Conversely, we prove that CHR can simulate Turing machines if an unrestricted number of atoms is allowed. Additionally, the study provides a Tmings-incomplete result, showing that any CHR program capable of halting on every possible input can be converted into an equivalent program that halts within linear time relative to the input size.

We investigate the alignment of galaxy spin direction dipoles as identified in the SDSS DR12 catalog, utilizing a methodology previously applied to the 2dFGRS and DESI-NGC surveys. Our analysis reveals that the dipole axes derived from DR12 are consistent with those from prior surveys, with the primary distinction being a difference in the axes' orientations. This discrepancy is attributed to variations in the survey volumes covered by each dataset. Furthermore, we examine the alignment of spin directions within galaxy clusters, specifically targeting the Coma cluster. Our results indicate that the spin directions of galaxies in Coma are not randomly oriented; rather, they exhibit a preferred direction that aligns with the cluster's velocity dispersion.

Few-shot learning (FSL) has emerged as a critical area of research, driven by the need to rapidly learn from limited labeled data. Although recent advances in metric-based FSL have yielded promising results, these methods often struggle with sampling bias and label noise, issues that can severely hinder performance. To address this, we introduce Eigen-Reptile, a novel feature-based FSL approach that utilizes the eigenspace of a feature matrix to generate a more stable and robust feature embedding. By leveraging this framework, Eigen-Reptile effectively mitigates sampling bias and label noise, leading to significant improvements in performance. Empirical evaluations across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that Eigen-Reptile surpasses state-of-the-art methods, achieving gains of up to 10% on the few-shot classification task.

This study introduces a novel deep learning framework designed to predict cognitive performance in Alzheimer's disease (AD) patients by leveraging MRI data. The proposed approach utilizes a multi-task learning strategy to simultaneously forecast future Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) scores and identify regions of interest (ROIs) exhibiting significant MMSE score changes. The system comprises two interconnected networks: a feature extraction module that processes MRI data alongside a multi-task learning module that integrates the ROIs identified by the first stage to generate predictions. Evaluated on the ADNI dataset, the model achieved an MMSE prediction accuracy of 0.71, outperforming the baseline accuracy of 0.67.

We argue that AI Ethics should be grounded in cognitive science, as this provides a robust framework for analyzing the moral dimensions of artificial intelligence. We further contend that the field would benefit from adopting a narrative-driven methodology, which facilitates the analysis of ethical issues in AI. The study of Boolean-closed full trios of language sets has been a prominent area in automata theory, notably because every such trio can be defined by a monadic second-order logic theory over word structures. This paper investigates the decidable Boolean-closed full trios specifically for languages defined over infinite word sets ($\omega$-words). We demonstrate that the trio containing co-finite languages is the unique decidable one for these infinite inputs. This result resolves an open question previously raised by Pin and Thierrin.

This study introduces a hybrid channel estimation framework designed to enhance performance in millimeter-wave (mmWave) systems. The approach integrates a deep neural network (DNN) with least squares (LS) channel estimation. Specifically, the DNN is trained to forecast the channel impulse response (CIR) by utilizing the CIR estimated via LS as input. Simulation outcomes demonstrate that this hybrid method achieves superior accuracy compared to conventional LS estimation alone.

Recent discrepancies between experimental results and Standard Model predictions for $V_{ud}$ and $V_{us}$ offer compelling evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. This work examines the impact of such new interactions on the radiative decay of muons, specifically calculating the $\mathcal{O}(m_\mu/M_W)$ corrections to the decay rate and the $(m_\ell^2/m^2_{W})$-suppressed contributions to the electron-to-muon ratio decay $R_{e/\mu}$.

This study introduces a new approach for generating high-quality, high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. The proposed architecture employs a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) that integrates dilated kernels to capture extensive contextual information, while a sub-network based on the U-Net design facilitates the progressive reconstruction of image details. The model was trained on the CelebA dataset, which consists of 10,000 pairs of aligned low-resolution and high-resolution facial images. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR).

Data views are frequently utilized to present information from a database, yet they often leak private data alongside shared details. This paper addresses the challenge of separating private and shared views within a database. We demonstrate that determining the feasibility of this separation is NP-hard. Furthermore, we prove that if an efficient separation exists, an efficient reconstruction is also possible. We introduce a randomized algorithm that achieves view reconstruction with a failure probability of no more than 1/3.

This study examines the correlation between hot dust emission and the physical characteristics of galaxies within the local universe. Utilizing data from the Spitzer Space Telescope, we analyzed 1,000 galaxies from the Spitzer Infrared Galaxy Survey (SINGS) that have been classified morphologically. We employed a two-component model to fit the Spitzer spectral energy distributions (SEDs), separating contributions from cold and hot dust. Our results indicate that the bolometric luminosity of hot dust correlates with the radio luminosity of the host galaxies, suggesting that hot dust primarily originates from radio-loud galaxies. Furthermore, we observed that galaxies with hot dust tend to exhibit disturbed morphologies, implying that such features are a common characteristic of these systems.

Although large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in various domains, their ability to handle human moral reasoning remains limited. This study introduces MORALCOT, a novel prompting strategy designed to enhance LLMs for moral tasks. By leveraging a chain-of-thought framework, MORALCOT encourages the model to reason through a sequence of steps: first, it identifies relevant moral principles; next, it applies these to the specific scenario; and finally, it generates a moral judgment. This structured reasoning process enables the model to better grasp the complexities of human moral decision-making. We evaluated the method using the HARM-LLM benchmark, which assesses LLMs on their ability to align with human values and moral standards. Our findings indicate that MORALCOT significantly improves performance on HARM-LLM, surpassing the best-performing base model by 10.4% in zero-shot settings. Furthermore, the model's intermediate reasoning steps offer valuable insights into its decision-making logic.

The 2D Dirac equation is highly relevant across various fields, including condensed matter physics, quantum chemistry, and high-energy physics. This study introduces a new finite difference method designed for solving 2D Dirac equations with time-varying coefficients. The approach utilizes a split-step technique to discretize the equation, treating the time-dependent mass term separately from the remaining components. Spatial discretization is handled via the finite difference method, while a central difference scheme approximates the time-variable mass term. The resulting algorithm is proven to be stable, and numerical experiments confirm its effectiveness.

Model Predictive Control (MPC) has proven effective in optimizing cooperative driving scenarios, such as platoon formation and lane changes. However, its computational demands often restrict its use in real-time applications. This paper introduces a novel MPC framework that integrates Model Predictive Path Adaption (MPPA) to enhance computational efficiency. The proposed approach employs a linearized dynamic model to derive analytical solutions for the underlying quadratic program, thereby eliminating the need for iterative numerical solvers. Additionally, a new prediction horizon strategy is developed to ensure the system's robustness against model inaccuracies and external disturbances. Simulation results demonstrate that this method significantly improves computational speed without compromising control performance.

The rapid proliferation of social media has created an information environment characterized by an overwhelming volume of content, making it increasingly difficult for users to assess credibility. This challenge is exacerbated by the fact that individuals often rely on others' opinions to form their own views, a behavior that can amplify misinformation when influenced by biased or unreliable sources. To address this, we introduce a novel framework designed to identify trustworthy information sources. Our approach utilizes a graph neural network to analyze the network of social connections, enabling the system to assess the credibility of a source based on the opinions of its neighbors. Empirical results demonstrate that this method effectively identifies reliable information providers.

The proposed $\pi$-ROAD framework enables road emergency management operators to monitor, analyze, and manage traffic data in real time. It achieves this by leveraging the dynamic nature of road networks and the spatiotemporal characteristics of traffic flow. Specifically, $\pi$-ROAD assists operators in three key areas: (1) identifying traffic incidents and predicting traffic conditions to optimize resource allocation; (2) visualizing traffic data to support decision-making; and (3) analyzing traffic patterns to inform long-term traffic management strategies.

This study introduces a collaborative approach for managing multiple robots within a shared workspace. The core of the framework involves a multi-agent Markov Decision Process (MADP) designed to optimize the joint trajectories of all robots, while integrating an artificial potential fields (APF) collision avoidance method to prevent interactions. We demonstrate that this combination results in shorter overall completion times for the assigned tasks. Furthermore, we validate the framework's effectiveness through simulations involving two robots tasked with moving an object from a starting to a final destination.

The trajectory of urban development is being reshaped by the convergence of heightened autonomy and machine intelligence. As these technologies advance, they will fundamentally alter the built environment, transportation systems, and the daily routines of city inhabitants. This paper examines the disruptive potential of these advancements on the future of urbanism, exploring how they might redefine the very essence of the city.

This paper introduces the Trilateral Attention Network (TANet), a novel architecture designed for image segmentation. TANet integrates three distinct pathways: a global pathway, a semantic pathway, and a local pathway. The global pathway leverages the self-attention mechanism to capture long-range dependencies, while the semantic pathway utilizes a self-attention module to extract high-level semantic features. The local pathway employs a self-attention mechanism to focus on fine details. By combining these three pathways, the model generates a comprehensive representation of the input image. Experiments conducted on the PASCAL-Context and Cityscapes datasets demonstrate that TANet achieves state-of-the-art results, surpassing existing methods.

We examine the gauge structure of linearized supergeometry within the framework of $\mathcal{N}=1$ superspace. In this context, gauge transformations are defined by superfields that function as covariant generalizations of tensor fields. Specifically, we derive the torsion constraints applicable to the process of gauge fixing, demonstrating that these torsion conditions impose restrictions on how the gauge fields for linearized supergravity and supergravity interact. Furthermore, we analyze the constraints on curvature arising from the torsion relations and discuss their implications for the gravitational and supergravity gauge fields.

The quality of learning models relies heavily on the data used for training. However, in many scenarios, the data is noisy or corrupted, and the resulting models may fail to accurately reflect the underlying distribution. This paper introduces a method to evaluate data quality by analyzing the contribution of individual training examples to the final model. We demonstrate that this approach is highly effective for identifying noisy examples, offering a granular assessment of data quality that surpasses traditional metrics based solely on model performance. We validate this method using a variety of classification tasks, including those with noisy labels and those involving concept drift. Our findings indicate that the proposed metric is both computationally efficient and robust across different domains.

We investigate the quantum charge pumping mechanism in the three-dimensional surface of the 3D quantum anomalous Hall (QAHE) system, which is driven by the non-equilibrium dynamics of the Chern insulator. Our analysis demonstrates that the non-Abelian matrix Berry phase associated with the Chern insulator's edge states is the primary driver of this pumping process. Furthermore, we establish that the efficiency of charge pumping is governed by the magnitude of the Chern number.

We introduce the METRO LM family, a series of large language models that deliver state-of-the-art performance on various benchmarks using significantly fewer parameters than prior models. This efficiency is achieved through a novel architecture that integrates a Mixture of Experts (MoE) design with a dynamic sparse routing mechanism. Our models, which range from 128M to 1.6B parameters, are trained on a 100TB dataset of multilingual text. They achieve competitive results on standard tasks such as language modeling, translation, summarization, and question answering. Furthermore, we provide an open-source implementation of the 1.6B parameter model, which is available for download at https://huggingface.co/meta-llama/METRO-LM-1.6B.

We introduce a protocol for determining the topology of a quantum network composed of $N$ nodes, utilizing only local data gathered at each node. This method relies on a specific assumption: the network's topology is represented as a graph where every edge represents a quantum channel with a fidelity exceeding a defined threshold. By employing a novel, efficient algorithm, we can deduce the complete network structure from $N$ independent local datasets. This approach is particularly advantageous for large-scale networks, as it eliminates the need for complex, centralized data aggregation. Furthermore, the protocol is designed to be compatible with various physical platforms and communication technologies.

This research investigates how different introduction strategies influence the ability to explain visual encodings to viewers. We examined three distinct methods: (1) a textual approach, (2) a visual approach, and (3) a hybrid textual-visual approach. To evaluate their effectiveness, we conducted two experiments: one measuring the audience's comprehension of the explanation and another assessing the explainer's efficiency in generating explanations. The results indicate that while textual introductions are the most efficient for generating explanations, they are not the most effective for audience understanding; conversely, visual introductions significantly improve the audience's comprehension of the encodings.

The study of many-body quantum systems is advancing rapidly, driven by the creation of quantum simulators and computers. A key challenge in this field is understanding how quantum order emerges from disordered initial states. This paper examines the dynamics of order formation in a quantum spin chain subjected to periodic driving, a technique widely used in optical manipulation. We find that Floquet heating causes the system to enter a highly excited state, where the initial quantum order is lost. However, by carefully tuning the driving parameters, we can suppress this heating, allowing the initial order to persist for extended durations. This process enables the creation of Floquet states that exhibit a wide range of properties, including long-range order, short-range order, and long-range entanglement.

Counterfactual reasoning is a powerful method for generating plans to achieve specific goals. This paper introduces a novel approach that integrates counterfactuals with reinforcement learning (RL) to create plans resilient to uncertainty in model parameters. We demonstrate that when model parameters are imperfectly known, a counterfactual plan derived from the true underlying model may prove ineffective. To address this, we propose a method that learns a policy capable of generating counterfactual plans that maintain performance even when the true parameters are inaccurate. We show that this strategy surpasses existing methods in both model-based and reinforcement learning contexts.

This study introduces a novel approach for classifying urban sounds that leverages a pre-trained convolutional neural network originally designed for image recognition. The methodology involves converting audio waveforms into spectrograms and subsequently processing these visual representations through the image-based neural network. Experimental evaluations conducted on the ESC-50 and US8k datasets yielded accuracies of 85.7% and 90.7%, respectively.

This paper introduces SCAMP-5, a compiler designed for the 5th generation of superconducting analog quantum computers. It facilitates the development of quantum programs in Python, compiling them into low-level instruction sets that drive hardware analog evolution. The SCAMP-5 language supports both linear and non-linear Hamiltonians, with the latter capable of handling time-dependent and non-commutative terms. The tool includes a comprehensive instruction set tailored for analog quantum systems, featuring a new compiler optimization strategy that minimizes gate execution time by leveraging commutation relations. Additionally, a detailed description of the SCAMP-5 language and compiler is provided, along with a comparative analysis against prior implementations. This evaluation covers the compiler's code generation efficiency, specifically comparing the output size of SCAMP-5 against other compilers, and assesses its performance on standard benchmarks.

We examine the generalized Witten effect within the framework of quantum gravity, demonstrating that it imposes significant constraints on the charge spectrum of massive states. Specifically, we derive a spectrum rule that limits the number of available charged states for any given electric charge $q$. This rule scales inversely with the square root of the Planck mass, $M_{\rm Pl}$, expressed as $N(q) \lesssim q/M_{\rm Pl}^{1/2}$. By applying this rule to the moduli space of $SU(N)$ $N$-instanton solutions in Yang-Mills theory, we establish an upper bound on the instanton number that is consistent with established existence theorems.

We introduce two new variations of regret pruning that enhance the original approach by incorporating a novel regularization term. This term is derived from the mean squared distance between the average trajectory of play and the nearest equilibrium. We prove that this addition ensures the algorithm converges to the closest solution among those available, rather than just any equilibrium. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these new variations achieve faster convergence rates compared to the original method. We also provide an algorithm for computing Nash equilibria that leverages these new variations. Empirical results indicate that our regret pruning implementation outperforms established baselines such as Counterfactual Regret Minimization (CFR) and its improved variants.

We present a novel modal logic that extends the author's prior propositional logic, which was formulated using the framework of possible states-of-affairs. This system is designed to clarify the semantics of Aristotle's modal syllogistic by demonstrating how it governs the truth conditions of premises and conclusions across varying possible states-of-affairs.

Causal inequalities serve as tools to determine whether observed correlations arise from classical or quantum causes. While quantum and classical causal models can be distinguished through respective inequalities violated by them, a key distinction lies in the detection efficiency required to breach these inequalities: violating classical versions demands a higher efficiency threshold than violating quantum ones. This study examines a specific subset of classical causal models, termed "causally separable with a fixed order," where a specific causal order between measurements is predetermined. We demonstrate that these models can be fully characterized by a specific class of quantum inequalities, meaning any violation of these quantum inequalities necessarily implies the underlying model is not classically restricted to this fixed order.

This study introduces a dual-critic reinforcement learning framework designed to manage video encoding by jointly optimizing rate-distortion (RD) performance and computational complexity. By utilizing two distinct action spaces, the framework simultaneously addresses rate constraints and complexity limits. Two separate value functions are employed to assess the RD and complexity components, respectively, with reinforcement learning algorithms updating these functions alongside the policy network. Experiments conducted on the HEVC test sequences using the VVC reference software demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior RD efficiency compared to the baseline, yielding improvements of up to 1.4 dB at fixed complexity levels. Furthermore, the framework effectively adapts to varying encoder complexities, offering a viable solution for encoding under complexity restrictions.

This study investigates the impact of carbon-rich grain photo-ablation on the gas-phase chemistry within protoplanetary disks. We introduce a new chemical model that incorporates the photodissociation of these grains, which releases carbon atoms into the gas phase. This process is integrated into a chemical network featuring a novel set of reactions, including the formation of C$_2$H$_2$ and C$_2$H$_4$ from C$_2$H, as well as the production of C$_3$N$_2$ and C$_3$H$_2$ from CN and CH. We demonstrate that the photo-ablation of carbon-rich grains sustains a prolonged equilibrium cycle in the gas-phase chemistry of protoplanetary disks. This cycle involves the formation of C$_2$H$_2$ and C$_2$H$_4$ from C$_2$H, as well as the production of C$_3$N$_2$ and C$_3$H$_2$ from CN and CH. This study introduces NeuralCut, a deep learning framework designed to automate cut selection in mixed-integer linear programming (MILP). By leveraging a neural network to identify and add cuts, Neuralcuts aims to accelerate solution times for these models. Our approach utilizes a graph-based representation of MILP structures, enabling the model to learn cut selection strategies directly from solver states. Experimental results demonstrate that, when compared to current best practices, our method surpasses traditional baseline approaches in 80% of test cases. Additionally, it exceeds the performance of existing neural network models by achieving a 20% improvement in solution speed.

We report on the synthesis of the ternary compound T$_d$-Mo$_{x}$Ir$_{x}$Te$_{x}$ and its superconducting properties. This study reveals that the superconducting transition temperature ($T_c$) increases with iridium concentration, reaching a maximum of $T_c = 10.2$ K at $x = 0.1$. The superconductivity is characterized by an isotropic, s-wave symmetry, as evidenced by the absence of any anomalous behavior in the temperature dependence of the superfluid density. Additionally, the superfluid density remains nearly constant across the entire doping range, indicating that the superconducting mechanism is intrinsic to the material.

This study introduces a new approach to retrieve bug reports that are functionally identical to a submitted issue. While traditional methods rely on developers manually matching the reports based on their expertise, our proposed system leverages Natural Language Processing (NLP) to automate this process. By applying NLP techniques to identify reports with matching functionality, the system significantly enhances the ability to locate exact functional counterparts.

We examine the phase transitions in graphene through the framework of a strongly coupled effective field theory. This approach reveals that the theory is characterized by a supersymmetric renormalization group fixed point, which governs the infrared physics. Consequently, the theory's critical exponents are determined by those of an associated free supersymmetric theory. This connection allows for the calculation of critical exponents with high precision, matching the accuracy of recent experiments.

This paper introduces a self-teacher-student training framework designed to enhance Named Entity Recognition (NER) performance. The student model, built on a BERT-based architecture, is trained using a combination of labeled data and pseudo-labels generated by the teacher. The teacher's iterative updates are derived from its own outputs, augmented by the initial labeled dataset. Experiments conducted on the OntoNotes 5.0 and CoNLL2003 datasets demonstrate that this method significantly improves accuracy over both baseline models and existing state-of-the-art solutions.

The travel and hospitality sector has experienced significant growth, particularly in recent years, driven by the widespread adoption of social media. This shift has enabled travelers to share experiences, seek recommendations, and offer feedback on hotels and destinations. Consequently, tourism businesses can leverage this data to identify market trends, refine their offerings, and enhance customer service. This study examines the insights available from tourism-related social media posts, specifically focusing on the #travel and #travelgram hashtags. We conducted a comprehensive analysis of 10,000 tweets to uncover patterns and insights, ultimately demonstrating that these data can be utilized to forecast travel trends and support informed decision-making for the industry.

This study introduces a machine learning framework designed to forecast the effective properties of microstructured materials. The model utilizes the average values of microscopic fields—such as displacement, strain, and stress—as inputs to predict effective properties. To generate these inputs, the framework employs the heterogeneous multiscale method (HMM) alongside a finite element method (FEM). The core of the model is a neural network trained on a dataset comprising 1,000 distinct microstructures, each characterized by 1,000 randomly generated realizations. The network is trained to minimize the error between the predicted effective properties and the reference values obtained through direct numerical simulations. The resulting model demonstrates high accuracy and efficiency, with the training process requiring only a fraction of the computational resources needed for traditional simulations.

We report the detection of a companion to the young star CI Tau at a separation of 0.2 arcseconds, corresponding to a projected physical distance of 100 AU. This companion, identified as CI Tau c, has a mass of 0.015 solar masses and a projected orbital velocity of 1.5 km/s. The discovery of CI Tau c, which orbits at a much larger distance than the planet CI Tau b, rules out planet-induced migration as the cause of CI Tau b's current position. Furthermore, angular differential imaging at this resolution excludes a mass of 0.01 solar masses at 100 AU as a potential companion, thereby excluding the possibility of a binary system with a mass ratio of q = 0.01.

We demonstrate a correspondence linking zero-energy trajectories of a specific potential in flat space to finite-energy trajectories of free movement on a sphere. This correspondence is established through a stereographic projection of the planar orbit onto the spherical surface.

This paper examines the existence of non-trivial solutions for non-local integro-differential equations featuring indefinite $p(x)$-Laplacians. By utilizing a non-local energy functional approach, we derive conditions based on the spectral theory associated with these equations. Specifically, the presence of at least two distinct solutions is guaranteed when the first eigenvalue of the corresponding linearized operator separates the spectrum of the functional into its positive and negative regions.

This study introduces a novel approach to unlabelled multi-object filtering that integrates a particle filter with Rao-Blackwellised Gibbs sampling. The methodology employs a particle filter to approximate the posterior distribution of object labels, while utilizing Gibbs sampling to refine this approximation for the remaining stochastic variables. This combination enables the use of extended target models, which are particularly advantageous when dealing with sparse detections. Furthermore, the proposed solution enhances trajectory estimation capabilities by allowing for data association across multiple time steps. The algorithm's efficacy is demonstrated through simulations involving a mobile robot navigating an indoor environment, where it successfully estimates trajectories for a subset of targets despite the presence of clutter.

This paper introduces a new stability assessment criterion for large-scale power systems with extensive converter penetration, utilizing a two-time-scale decomposition approach. By integrating synchronous machines and converters into a unified framework, the authors derive a linearized model that captures the interaction between these devices. This model is subsequently employed to formulate a stability metric based on the energy function, which is validated through a case study on a 39-bus system.

This study introduces a novel signature forgery detection approach utilizing machine learning. The proposed method relies on three signature templates: a genuine specimen, a known authentic sample, and a specimen under investigation. These templates are generated from a single handwritten signature, with the known authentic sample created by a specific writer. The framework employs a deep learning model to assess the distinctiveness, complexity, and repeatability of the respective signature samples. The widespread adoption of smartphones has driven a surge in mobile application usage, prompting the need for more personalized experiences. To achieve this, it is essential to understand user context, which can be captured through various data sources. This paper introduces a new approach to modeling user context by leveraging the contextual values found in mobile app stores. By persistently storing these values, we can build a comprehensive profile of user context that enables the customization of mobile applications.

This paper introduces a novel 3D pose estimation framework that delivers real-time performance by leveraging a multi-scale feature pyramid and a dual-branch architecture. The system employs a feature pyramid to extract multi-scale representations, which are subsequently processed by a dual-branch design to predict 3D joint coordinates and joint confidence scores. The model is trained using a joint loss function that integrates Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Cross-Entropy (CE) losses. Furthermore, we implemented a data augmentation strategy to enhance robustness against occlusion and pose variations. The framework was evaluated on the Human3.6M dataset, where it achieved a Mean Per-Joint-Position Error (MPJPE) of 61.4 mm and a Confidence Error (CE) of 0.013.

This study details the calibration of the INS, covering its energy response, point spread function, and spectral resolution. This paper introduces a formal framework for classifying blockchain protocols based on their consensus mechanisms, specifically distinguishing between permissioned and permissionless systems. For permissionless protocols, we define a formal model of anonymous participants capable of proposing and advancing blocks, which we utilize to establish a formal proof of the double-spending vulnerability inherent in such systems. Conversely, we develop a formal model for permissioned systems featuring identified participants, demonstrating that this model is inherently resilient against double-spending attacks. Finally, we apply these models to validate the security properties of selected blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Hyperledger Fabric, and PBFT.

We have recently introduced a refined chromomagnetic interaction (AMI) model that successfully reproduces the mass spectra of both spin-0 and spin-1 charmonium-like states, $X_{0}(3872)$, and $X_{1}(3872)$, as well as the lightest bottomonium-like particles, $Y_{0}(10860)$ and $Y_{1}(10940)$. This study examines the stability scale within a scalar extension of the Standard Model, specifically a model featuring a complex scalar field with a general potential. We derive the full one-loop renormalization group equations and analyze the resulting stability conditions. Our results indicate that, in contrast to the Standard Model, the scale of instability is not constrained by limits on the Higgs mass. Furthermore, we demonstrate that within the framework of the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), the instability scale can be determined solely from low-energy observables.

This study demonstrates that the Hamilton-Jacobi equation admits a solution in Carnot groups satisfying the $\sigma$-Talagrand inequality. This finding extends the work presented by the same authors in their article "Solutions of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation in spaces with talagrand inequality," published in the Journal of Geometric Analysis in 2020.

This study introduces a novel estimator, termed Exponentially Weighted Divergence (EWD), which is designed to be computationally efficient and robust. We demonstrate that the EWD estimator can be derived as a specific instance of the density power divergence (DPD) class, yet it is computable via a straightforward recursive formula. Our analysis reveals that this estimator is not only more precise than DPD but also offers superior computational speed. Furthermore, we establish that EWD is a consistent estimator of the true density. We also examine its behavior under model misspecification and establish its robustness. Additionally, we derive the asymptotic distribution of EWD, which is essential for constructing confidence intervals. Finally, our extensive simulations and real-world applications confirm that EWD is a highly effective tool for density estimation.

This study introduces a new algorithm designed to enhance image quality by distinguishing between static and motion-centric pixels, followed by selectively applying specific filters to each category. The approach utilizes a novel pixel classification technique that leverages the directional characteristics of motion. Additionally, it integrates a dedicated motion detection mechanism to identify and process motion-oriented pixels. By applying directional filtering to static areas and traditional noise reduction to motion-focused regions, the method effectively suppresses noise while maintaining the integrity of moving objects. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques in terms of both noise reduction and the preservation of motion details.

This paper investigates the link between the spectral statistics of periodic graphs and the geometric characteristics of their corresponding periodic orbits. We demonstrate that coefficients in the characteristic polynomial of a periodic graph are more volatile when the orbit contains self-intersections compared to when it does not. Furthermore, we prove that the spectral variance of a generic periodic graph is higher in the presence of such self-intersections. We also examine the implications of these findings for the arithmetic properties of these graphs.

We introduce a new classification system for periodic variable stars, developed using a supervised machine learning approach. This system categorizes variables into two groups: (1) eclipsing binaries and (2) nebular variables (NEB). The model was trained on a dataset of 1,000 light curves, comprising 500 real observations and 500 synthetic curves. The results demonstrate that the classifier effectively distinguishes between these groups, achieving an accuracy of 98.5%. The classifier's performance is robust across various periods, amplitudes, and duty cycles. Additionally, we applied this tool to a sample of 1,000 real periodic variables from the OGLE-IV catalog, successfully identifying 98.5% of the true nebular variables and 98.5% of the true eclipsing binaries within those subsets.

This study addresses the characterization of the closest nearest negative imaginary system to a given linear time invariant (LTI) system featuring real rational transfer functions. It establishes that for a known non-negative imaginary system, the closest candidate is uniquely identified by applying a specific projection operation onto the space of negative imaginary systems. Furthermore, the work presents a method for calculating this projection for systems exhibiting any form of imaginary symmetry. These findings are demonstrated through multiple illustrative examples.

This study evaluates the efficacy of continual learning in End-to-End Automatic Speech Recognition (E2E-ASR) by employing various algorithms to train a single E2E-ASR model incrementally across multiple data domains. The research compares these methods against a baseline of fine-tuning a pre-trained model on new tasks. The findings indicate that the top-performing continual learning approach surpasses the baseline fine-tuning by 10% relative improvement on new tasks, while simultaneously retaining 95% of the performance on prior tasks. Additionally, the paper introduces a novel metric designed to assess the degree of catastrophic forgetting in ASR systems.

Sentiment analysis is a vital component of social media analytics, yet it faces significant hurdles when dealing with code-switching messages prevalent in Sino-Speech contexts. This study introduces a novel approach to address this challenge by employing a dual neural network architecture: one network processes Chinese text while the other handles English. We utilize a BERT-based model for each language stream and integrate their respective embeddings through a specialized fusion mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed framework outperforms current state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior F1-scores on the CodeSwitching Sentiment Analysis (CSA) dataset.

This study examines the three-loop neutrino seesaw model, which generates small neutrino masses through intricate fermion loop corrections involving heavy neutral leptons. We demonstrate that this framework permits a normal ordering of neutrino masses and successfully accommodates both baryon and lepton asymmetries of the universe. Furthermore, we analyze the model's predictions for dark matter, finding that it allows for a viable WIMP candidate. Specifically, we show that the scalar mediator within this model can be lighter than 129 GeV, making it potentially detectable through current dark matter experiments.

Product-based Neural Networks (PNNs) are increasingly utilized in tabular data analysis, yet their underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study introduces a theoretical framework for PNNs, elucidating how their architecture captures interactions among categorical variables and manages their representations. We establish that PNNs can model any interaction pattern between fields, and that the capacity to represent these fields is contingent upon the specific parameterization of the input encoding. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a specific PNN configuration can replicate the functionality of traditional statistical models. These insights offer a foundation for developing more effective PNN architectures.

This study examines active transmitting beamforming design for a hybrid active/passive intelligent reflecting surface (HRIS)-assisted communication network. By integrating the distinct capabilities of active reflection and direct transmission, this architecture addresses the limitations of traditional passive RIS, which cannot compensate for channel estimation errors. Specifically, we formulate an optimization problem to maximize the minimum rate of all users under CSI uncertainty constraints. To resolve this non-convex challenge, we introduce a novel block coordinate descent algorithm that alternates between optimizing the hybrid surface's reflection/transmission coefficients and adjusting the user-specific beamforming vectors. Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms benchmark solutions in terms of computational efficiency and performance.

Branch prediction is a critical component of modern CPUs, and while conventional methods rely on simple history-based mechanisms, emerging approaches leverage deep learning to enhance accuracy. This study introduces a new predictor that integrates the classic 2-bit, 2-history scheme with a deep neural network. This hybrid design utilizes deep learning to refine predictions based on historical branch patterns, effectively addressing the context-agnostic limitations of traditional models. Experimental results indicate that our proposed method outperforms both standard predictors and those exclusively powered by deep learning.

This paper introduces a deep convolutional neural network designed to autonomously manage a camera's movement and positioning. The system utilizes image data alongside target coordinates to generate camera control commands, eliminating the need for a 3D depth sensor or explicit 3D spatial mapping. This approach is particularly advantageous in scenarios where 3D sensors are unavailable or impractical, such as in industrial settings. The model is trained on a physical robotic platform equipped with a depth camera and a 3D laser scanner, yet it learns to perform tracking using only RGB imagery. Experimental results demonstrate that the system achieves robust target monitoring across various challenges, including occlusion and movement, while maintaining superior performance compared to benchmark methods.

We investigate the Ising SOS model on the upper half-space $\mathbb{Z}^{d+1}_+$, where the boundary is assigned a uniform measure. We demonstrate that the resulting boundary laws are not normalizable, thereby ruling out the possibility of a pure phase. Furthermore, we prove that the model exhibits a unique overall phase.

This study introduces a novel approach to characterize entangled two-photon resonance energy transfer (E2P) using ultrafast spectroscopy. The method relies on a unique two-color pump-probe scheme that employs a broadband probe pulse to generate a specific frequency shift, thereby enabling the detection of E2P signals. By applying this technique to the DNA base pair guanine-cytosine (GC), we successfully measured the E2P rate coefficient ($K_{E2P}$) for the first time. The results indicate that the E2P process in GC is driven by a vibrational resonance between the donor and acceptor molecules. Furthermore, we observed a significant reduction in $K_{E2P}$ when the vibrational resonance condition was disrupted by adjusting the temperature. These findings offer new insights into the mechanism of two-photon resonance energy transfer and its critical role in the ultrafast photodynamics of DNA.

We present a comprehensive review of the non-perturbative determination of the strong coupling constants, $\alpha_s$, utilizing light-cone QCD sum rules. This approach yields values that align closely with other non-perturbative methods, such as the running coupling constant derived from the beta function and the strong coupling constant inferred from quarkonium systems.

The anomalous results from short-baseline neutrino oscillation experiments, including the MiniBooNE and the recently added MicroBooNE data, are examined. We demonstrate that within the framework of the minimal extended Standard Model, which includes both a dark photon and a sterile neutrino, these phenomena can be resolved. This solution is achieved by adjusting the neutrino's mass scale to the GeV range and employing a sterile neutrino mixing angle of approximately $10^{-3}$.

The challenge of estimating causal effects from observational data is a central focus in both statistics and causal inference. While regression techniques are commonly employed to adjust for confounding variables, they are often criticized for being overly sensitive to violations of the model's linearity assumption. This paper proposes a new approach to observational study design by utilizing the implicit weights generated by linear regression methods. We demonstrate that these weights can be restructured into a weighted propensity score model, which facilitates the design of studies that are robust to non-linear confounding effects. We validate this method through a simulation study and apply it to a real-world dataset concerning the impact of air pollution on mortality rates.

The proposed approach utilizes a control framework that integrates a model-based controller with a data-driven controller. The model-based controller is designed to regulate system oscillations by modulating the active power output of the VSCs, whereas the data-driven component addresses the nonlinear characteristics of the system. The methodology begins by constructing a linearized model of the multi-VSC power system. Subsequently, an optimal state feedback controller is derived using Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) design principles to stabilize the system. We introduce a theoretical framework for analyzing photon statistics emitted by a multi-atomic ensemble. This formalism utilizes a generalized $n$-atomic Green's function to establish a direct link between photon correlation functions and the time evolution of atomic energy correlations. Consequently, phenomena such as photon bunching, which arise from decay processes involving pairs of atoms, are readily identified. Furthermore, the theory facilitates the calculation of scattering amplitudes for light interacting with the group. We apply this approach to investigate the scattering of light from a two-atom system, demonstrating that it accurately reproduces established results from prior literature.

This study examines the stability of kink solutions within models featuring internal modes. We demonstrate that internal modes can destabilize kinks, deriving a stability criterion that aligns with our numerical findings. Furthermore, we explore the impact of external perturbations on kink stability.

Generalized parton distributions (GPDs) are essential for understanding high-energy hadron interactions and the three-dimensional spatial structure of nucleons. This study examines the connection between GPDs and hadron production by analyzing the high-energy behavior of $f_0(980)$-proton scattering. We determine the coupling constants for $f_0(980)$-proton interactions using the high-energy limits of the scattering amplitude, which are expressed in terms of the $f_0(980)$ contributions to the proton's GPDs. Furthermore, we evaluate the significance of these GPD-derived contributions in generating neutral pions via the process $p + f_0(980) \rightarrow p + \pi^0$.

Text classification is a critical natural language processing task with extensive applications, yet the robustness of these models against text perturbations remains a significant concern. This study introduces a novel training framework that enhances robustness by incorporating discrete noise into the training process. Unlike prior approaches that rely on a separate adversarial model, this method directly integrates noise generation into the training loss function. The proposed noise is designed to be task-aware, varying based on the specific classification objective. Experiments demonstrate that the resulting decision boundaries are both more robust and distinct. Furthermore, the approach achieves competitive performance across various datasets and tasks, including sentiment analysis, while offering computational efficiency that surpasses existing adversarial training techniques.

Polyp detection is a critical component in endoscopy, a field where the need for high precision and efficiency is paramount. While recent deep learning approaches have achieved remarkable results, they often struggle with the high computational costs associated with processing video data. To address this, we introduce a new architecture designed to enhance polyp detection in video sequences. Our approach employs a channel-aware attention mechanism that aggregates features from the current frame alongside those from preceding frames, thereby strengthening the network's ability to identify polyps. Furthermore, we utilize a multi-scale feature fusion strategy to ensure the model can detect polyps of varying sizes. Additionally, we propose a new loss function that specifically targets the challenge of detecting small polyps. Extensive experiments on the Kvasir-SEG dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This work introduces a sequential sampling approach that generates a random variable $X$ from a mixture of a normal distribution and a point mass at zero. By calibrating the probability of selecting the discrete zero value, we control the overall dispersion of $X$. The sampling algorithm is straightforward, with a computational cost of $O(1)$, and its variance can be set to any desired magnitude.

The rp-process, occurring during Type-I X-ray bursts, is characterized by the rapid proton capture of unstable nuclei. This study utilizes a Monte Carlo framework to simulate the process, incorporating nuclear reaction rates derived from both experimental data and theoretical models. The analysis focuses on the burst event GRS 1915+105, which is notable for its exceptionally high peak temperature. The results indicate that approximately 10% of the rp-process flow bypasses the waiting point $^{56}$Ni, while roughly 90% of the material proceeds past this point. The abundance of the final product nuclei is found to be highly sensitive to the reaction rates involving the nuclei $^{56}$Ni and $^{56}$Co.

We demonstrate that within a family of flat, closed subvarieties of an abelian scheme, the flat part can be characterized by its torsion cosets. Specifically, these irreducible components are defined as translates of abelian subvarieties by translates from the closed points of a scheme over which the base is defined. This result extends findings by Poonen and Vo regarding curves over number fields and by Cadman regarding linear systems on abelian varieties. Furthermore, we establish that any such family is topologically closed under specialization.

Over the past twenty years, Very High Energy (VHE) gamma-ray observations have significantly reshaped our understanding of the Milky Way's gamma-ray origins. This review outlines the current comprehension of the most significant VHE-emitting galactic sources, including pulsars, pulsar wind nebulae, supernova remnants, star-forming regions, and galactic nuclei.

This study examines the large-time behavior of a diffusion system within a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ subject to nonlocal boundary conditions. Specifically, we establish a representation formula for the solution's density and demonstrate that this system possesses a spectral gap. Furthermore, we derive an explicit formula for the stationary distribution and quantify the exponential rate of convergence toward equilibrium. These findings are achieved through the application of the probabilistic method.

We present a new method for classifying compact stellar systems (CSS) that leverages the color information from the CSS's surrounding environment. This approach utilizes a convolutional neural network (CNN) trained on a dataset of 1,000 CSS images, each sized 128x128 pixels. The training set consists of 800 labeled images (700 for training and 100 for validation) and includes 200 additional images for testing. The network was trained to distinguish between globular clusters (GCs) and globular cluster candidates (GC candidates) using the surrounding colors from the RGB and near-infrared bands. Our results indicate that the RGB bands are the most effective for classification, followed by the near-infrared bands. The method achieved an accuracy of 98.5% on the training set and 98.0% on the validation set. When applied to the test set, the network achieved an accuracy of 97.5%. This paper introduces a novel hypothesis testing method applicable to distributions with potentially infinite mean or variance, utilizing truncated sample means. We demonstrate that under mild conditions, these estimators are asymptotically normal, enabling the construction of confidence intervals and hypothesis tests. The approach is validated through simulations and a practical analysis of income data from the U.S. Census Bureau.

Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have demonstrated significant potential in the field of Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs). However, CNNs suffer from a lack of interpretability and require substantial amounts of labeled data for training. To address these limitations, this study introduces a new approach that integrates the interpretability of the Riemannian manifold with the data efficiency of CNNs. The proposed method involves a two-stage process: first, a CNN extracts features from raw EEG signals, and subsequently, these features are classified using Riemannian-based classifiers. The architecture is designed to be modular, allowing for the seamless replacement of individual components. Experimental results indicate that this hybrid framework achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art pure-CNN models while offering enhanced interpretability.

This study examines how the $AdS/CFT$ correspondence functions for a massive scalar field within a noncommutative space. We identify a dual $d+1$-dimensional gravitational theory that describes a massive scalar field interacting with a specific set of $d$-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge fields. Furthermore, we analyze the holographic entanglement entropy for this system, deriving an explicit formula for the entropy of a massive scalar field in noncommutative $d+1$-dimensional Anti-de Sitter space.

Kidney transplantation remains the optimal treatment for end-stage renal disease, yet post-transplant outcomes are heavily influenced by patient-organ mismatch. While clinical experts routinely assess compatibility across multiple dimensions, current MDP models for kidney allocation typically account only for blood type compatibility. This study introduces a novel MDP framework that expands the state representation to include incompatibility as a distinct state variable. This modification enables the modeling of intricate, multi-source incompatibilities and their associated risks. Furthermore, we propose a new "incompatibility penalty" metric to quantify the severity of these risks, which is subsequently employed to evaluate how such risks impact organ allocation policies.

This study investigates the geometric characteristics of Hidden Markov Model (HMM) latent states, specifically examining their topological and metric properties. We demonstrate that these latent states, when equipped with a natural distance function, form a metric space possessing a finite covering dimension. Furthermore, we establish that the mapping from an HMM's latent states to an embedding space is bi-Lipschitz continuous, with a Lipschitz constant determined by the model's transition matrix. These findings are further supported by numerical experiments comparing HMMs with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, which reveal that HMM latent states exhibit a more uniform geometric structure compared to the diverse patterns found in LSTM states.

This study examines weighted Bergman spaces $A^2(w)$ and $H^2(\varphi)$ defined on the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, along with the operators $\mathcal{I}_{\varphi,\psi}:A^2(w)\to H^2(\varphi)$ and $\mathcal{I}_{\varphi,\psi}:H^2(\varphi)\to A^2(w)$, which are defined by the difference quotient $(\mathcal{I}_{\varphi,\psi}f)(z)=\frac{f(\psi(z))-\mathcal{I}_{\varphi,\psi}f(0)}{\varphi(z)-\mathcal{I}_{\varphi,\psi}0}$. We determine the conditions under which these operators are compact or belong to the Schatten $p$-class for $0 < p < \infty$. Furthermore, we establish the conditions for the complete compactness and complete Schatten $p$-class membership of their adjoints.

The article proposes that data analysis and tool development for high-energy physics experiments demand a new form of collaborative effort, termed "collaborative software production." This approach is designed to enable a diverse range of participants to contribute to the creation of shared software tools.

We define a generalized concept of Howe curves and demonstrate that they correspond to decomposed Richelot isogenies. This process involves the Richetot isogeny from a generalized curve to its corresponding decomposed version. We also provide an explicit formula for the Richelot isogeny from a generalized curve to its corresponding decomposed version.

We report the discovery of three novel magnetic hot subdwarfs, designated as V396 Lyr, V397 Lyr, and V400 Lyr, within the V396–V400 Lyr cluster. These objects exhibit effective temperatures ranging from 22,000 to 26,000 K and surface gravities between log g = 5.0 and 5.5. Spectroscopic analysis reveals that all three stars display strong magnetic fields, with measured mean magnetic strengths of 100 kG, 120 kG, and 140 kG, respectively. Furthermore, we observe that their hydrogen abundances are approximately 0.3 dex lower than current theoretical models predict. This discrepancy suggests that the hydrogen in these stars has been depleted via a mechanism other than standard nuclear fusion.

This study introduces a methodology for analyzing errors in matrix approximation by leveraging invariant matrix theory. The authors demonstrate that error analysis can be framed as an eigenvalue problem within this theoretical domain. A numerical example is provided to validate the proposed approach.

This study examines the distribution of Wikipedia article topics and investigates how hyperlink structures within the site facilitate navigation. We analyze both raw wikitext and rendered HTML to assess the extent of linked content, revealing that raw wikitext contains significantly fewer links than HTML. By analyzing the raw wikitext, we determine that the majority of Wikipedia's content is interconnected through hyperlinks. Furthermore, our findings indicate that the site's hyperlink network is highly topical, with a strong correlation between the subject matter of an article and its linked neighbors.

We introduce a novel method for creating polar domains within twisted bilayers, which can serve as a promising platform for advancing topological physics. By utilizing a tunable twist angle, we demonstrate that a twisted bilayer of polar domains can host polar domain walls with either a single or a double width. Furthermore, we show that these domain walls can be reconfigured into twisted boundary conditions, resulting in the emergence of topological edge states. This work establishes a new strategy for manipulating polar domain walls and provides a distinct approach for investigating topological phenomena in this field.

This study examines how light propagates in a static, spherically symmetric, non-flat universe filled with a perfect fluid, where the metric is defined by two functions. By analyzing null geodesics, we derive specific constraints on these functions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for certain function choices, null geodesics within this curved spacetime correspond exactly to those found in a flat universe.

We investigate the movement of a single colloid within a liquid crystal medium confined between an oscillatory wall and a parallel plane. The wall features alternating hills and wells, creating a wavy structure that, when actuated, generates longitudinal flow. This flow arises from the interaction between the liquid crystal's elastic properties and the wall's periodic geometry. We demonstrate that colloid trajectories are governed by a competition between this elastic-induced flow and the surrounding Stokes drag. Specifically, particles located near the wall follow paths that mirror the wall's undulations, whereas those further away move in the direction of the imposed flow.

The Roche limit defines the distance within which tidal forces are strong enough to disrupt a celestial body. While this concept is well-established for planets and moons, it is also critical for understanding the behavior of small solar system objects, such as asteroids. This study examines the theoretical and observational characteristics of the Roche limit, specifically focusing on the elongation of an asteroid and its subsequent evolution. Our findings indicate that an asteroid's elongation is inversely proportional to its distance from the Sun, a relationship that holds true for bodies well outside the Roche limit. Furthermore, we derived a formula for the time required for an asteroid to reach Roche limit disruption, a duration that is inversely proportional to the magnitude of tidal forces. Utilizing this theoretical framework, we analyzed observational data from 100 known contact binary asteroids to determine the Roche limit for each. Our results reveal that these limits span a range from 2.5 to 10.5 solar radii.

Machine learning (ML) and quantum computing (QC) are increasingly vital for addressing complex challenges in molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. This study introduces a hybrid ML-QC framework designed to accelerate MD simulations by incorporating rare conformational transitions. By utilizing a Markov state model (MSM) to capture these infrequent events, the proposed method significantly enhances sampling efficiency. The workflow involves training a deep neural network (DNN) on MD trajectories to identify reaction coordinates, followed by employing quantum algorithms to generate optimized transition pathways between distinct conformational states. The resulting ensemble of trajectories is then combined with the original data to construct a comprehensive MSM. The efficacy of this approach is demonstrated through simulations of alanine dipeptide, revealing that the method successfully uncovers distinct structural transitions that conventional MD simulations fail to detect.

We introduce MAPPIES, a newly developed Monte-Carlo code designed to model polarisation in X-ray and gamma-ray emissions from astrophysical sources. This tool enables the investigation of polarisation mechanisms and their evolution throughout the emission process. The paper details the code's architecture, validation, and application, demonstrating its utility in analyzing polarisation in both Compton scattering and synchrotron radiation.

This study examines how the seasonal development of sea-ice thickness categories evolves in response to the inclusion of open water, utilizing a one-dimensional, thermodynamic sea-ice model. The analysis employs a two-component framework consisting of a single category of thick ice and a single category of thin ice, with open water represented as a distinct state. The research demonstrates that the seasonal evolution of these categories can be effectively modeled using a linear stochastic differential equation driven by white noise. This approach facilitates the application of established statistical methods to derive the long-term probability distribution of ice thickness categories. The findings indicate that the inclusion of open water significantly alters the distribution's characteristics, specifically by reducing the likelihood of observing thick ice.

We analyze the arithmetic and geometric properties of two families of curves, $\mathbf X_{a,b,n,s}$ and $\mathbf Y_{n,s}$, which arise from specific coverings of Hermitian curves. Our investigation focuses on their rational points, canonical models, and canonical embeddings.

Singing voice synthesis has garnered significant attention in recent years, yet challenges persist in both commercial and academic settings. This paper introduces a novel singing voice synthesis framework that utilizes a single neural network to generate both the melody and lyrics from an input audio track. By employing a new loss function, the system is trained to produce pitch and rhythm that align closely with the source audio. Furthermore, the study evaluates the system's performance across various scenarios, including singing in different keys, tempo changes, and the synthesis of vocals for novel texts.

Frame-based cameras are susceptible to motion blur and require extensive computational resources for calibration, whereas event-based cameras offer a high-speed, low-light alternative that is less affected by motion blur. However, event-based systems suffer from calibration challenges due to their high temporal resolution. This paper introduces a unified calibration framework that aligns extrinsic parameters between frame-based and event-based sensors. By leveraging the complementary strengths of both technologies, our method enables the extrinsic calibration of frame-based cameras using event-based data. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach achieves precise extrinsic calibration with a significantly reduced number of parameters compared to existing methods.

Graph learning has proven effective in numerous scenarios, including social and e-commerce networks, recommender systems, and knowledge graphs. However, existing research predominantly relies on supervised or semi-supervised settings, where node labels are either fully known or partially available. This paper introduces a novel framework for graph learning under fully unsupervised conditions, where the only available information is the graph structure itself. We present a new algorithm called Graph Self-Supervised Learning (GSSL), which utilizes self-supervised techniques to derive node embeddings. These embeddings are then used to generate a graph representation that captures the network's essential characteristics. We evaluate GSSL on various real-world datasets and demonstrate that it effectively learns meaningful node embeddings and produces robust graph representations.

We demonstrate that the braid group acting on four strands on the Hilzebruch surface of degree two is isomorphic to the mapping class group on four homologically trivial loops on the 3-sphere. This result provides a method to construct exceptional collections on the Hirzebruch surface of degree two using braid group operators.

This study introduces a 3D guidance system for retinal surgery that utilizes a spotlight projector to indicate the critical foveal area. By leveraging the projector's mechanism, the system offers a cost-effective and straightforward approach to three-dimensional navigation. The proposed method utilizes a spotlight projector linked to a retinal camera, which captures images of the illuminated fovea. A deep learning model is then trained to identify the foveal position within these images. The system's efficacy was validated through a simulation involving 1,000 images generated from 50 distinct retinal scans, each containing a spotlight-projected fovea. The model achieved a mean absolute error of 0.19 mm and a 95% confidence interval of 0.38 mm.

We demonstrate that the product formula for $F$-polynomials can be expressed as a specific summation involving monomials derived from the roots of an associated quadratic equation. This result is applied to a quadratic identity for $F$-polynomials, which is subsequently utilized to prove a closed-form summation for the binomial transform of a family of Chebyshev polynomials.

The FIDO2 standard is a significant step in the broader goal of eliminating passwords. This paper introduces a method to enhance FIDO2's security by utilizing a distributed key repository, where the key is fragmented and stored across multiple servers. This distribution strategy mitigates single points of failure and bolsters resistance against sophisticated cyberattacks. To facilitate this, we propose a new protocol that enables distributed servers to collaboratively verify a user's knowledge of a secret without revealing the secret itself. This protocol leverages the Interactive Oracle Proofs (IOP) framework, specifically employing a PCP-based PCPP proof system alongside a proof of knowledge for a specific algebraic problem.

We demonstrate that a novel Weyl-Wigner framework, which is designed to represent the quantum physics of qubits fails, and we illustrate this shortcoming by showing its inability to properly handle the quantum mechanics of a single spin-1/2 particle.

This paper introduces a novel interface for video applications that enhances user autonomy by offering a "canvas" to manipulate various elements, including advertisements, thumbnails, and progress bars. We present a design concept where users can layer these components to create personalized, context-aware visualizations. Our approach is supported by a prototype and a preliminary study indicating user approval. Furthermore, we examine the broader implications of this interface, particularly regarding its potential to transform how users interact with video content.

This paper examines the expressive power of the $\pi$-calculus when equipped with a specific set of behavioural equivalences. We demonstrate that a specific fragment of the $\pi$-calculus, which excludes input prefixes constrained by guards, is capable of specifying behaviours that are incompatible with Reactive Turing Machines (RTMs)—a finding that extends to any fragment limited only to finitely executable behaviours. Furthermore, we establish that this inability holds true even when employing the most permissive equivalence relations, such as those based on strong and weak bisimulation. In contrast, we prove that a fully expressive $\pi$-calculus can successfully model the behaviour of any RTM.
We introduce a designed Gray code for ordered trees that advances from one tree to the next by applying a single elementary transformation known as an evert operation.

This paper details the track reconstruction process within the ALICE experiment, specifically for central Pb-Pb collisions at an interaction energy of 5.02 TeV center-of-mass energy. Due to the extreme density of charged particles generated in such heavy ion events, track finding is a demanding task. We describe the methodology used to reconstruct tracks in the inner tracking system, covering both the Silicon Pixel detector and the Silicon Drift Chamber. Furthermore, we present the resulting track performance metrics, including efficiency, momentum resolution, and various sources of systematic uncertainties.

This study introduces a novel time-discontinuous prismatic space-time (D-PST) approach designed to overcome limitations inherent in traditional finite-elements when applied to free-surface flow simulations. The method employs a prismatic geometry to extend the computational domain along the time dimension, effectively transforming a three-dimensional spatial problem into a four-dimensional problem within a space-time framework. Within this extended domain, a set of prismatic elements is constructed to discretize the volume. The resulting system of equations is solved using a discontinuous Galerkin formulation in time, coupled with a continuous Galerkin method in space. The efficacy of this approach is validated through numerical experiments involving both steady and unsteady free-surface flow scenarios.

A circular $k$-flow on a signed graph $\Gamma$ is defined as a circular $k$-assignment on its edges that respects the sign constraints. The presence of such a flow serves as a sufficient condition for the existence of a modulo $k$-orientation, though this relationship is not equivalent. This work establishes a direct connection by demonstrating that for signed graphs with maximum degree $\Delta$ where $\Delta < \frac{n}{2}-1$, a circular $k$-flow exists if and only if a modulo $k$-orientation exists.

This study addresses the Modular Subset Sum problem, which involves determining if a target value $t$ can be expressed as a linear combination of given positive integers $a_1, \dots, a_n$ modulo $m$. We present a deterministic algorithm that runs in $O(n + m)$ time, improving upon prior methods that required $O(n\log^2 n)$ time. Our approach is based on the observation that every instance of this problem possesses a solution where the count of coefficients is bounded by $O(\log n)$.
